uncited: Photometric Loss Optimization is a differentiable inverse rendering technique that refines scene parameters, camera poses, or geometry by minimizing the pixel-wise difference between rendered images and ground-truth observations.

It sets itself apart from joint optimization methods by isolating specific variables (e.g., poses or rigid transformations) while keeping the radiance field fixed, or by employing specialized regularization to handle dynamic or sparse representations, as detailed in its variants [7526-gradient-based-se-3-optimization.md][12699-test-time-photometric-optimization.md][16983-point-cloud-optimization-via-pointersect.md][19691-ray-based-photometric-loss-for-heat-kernel-textures.md].

The method often restricts ray sampling to high-confidence regions or uses masks to avoid artifacts from scene inaccuracies or occlusions [7526-gradient-based-se-3-optimization.md][12699-test-time-photometric-optimization.md].
